lines: Three sections on one panel: a sample and hold, a clock generator with saw, square and trigger outputs, and a noise source giving white, pink and slow random voltages
Attenuates the held voltage on its way to SH OUT, from silence at fully counter-clockwise to the full sampled value at fully clockwise; it comes after the hold, so it does not change what is sampled
Sets the clock rate from 0.3Hz to 30Hz, on a cubed curve that puts most of the travel at the slow end
While this is above 1V the sample and hold passes SH IN straight through; when it falls below 1V the last value is held
A rising edge here resets the clock's sawtooth core to zero wherever it had got to, which is how to syncopate the clock against another one
A rising edge here samples SH IN once and holds it, with no tracking in between edges
Adds to the CLOCK FREQ setting, a tenth of the full 30Hz span per volt in either direction, with the result held inside the 0.3Hz to 30Hz range
The voltage the sample and hold section captures
A 10V pulse 5ms long at each rising edge of SQ OUT
White noise from a random number generator, 20V peak to peak
The clock's sawtooth core, rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle
Pink noise, the white noise source put through three filter stages; its level is a little below the white output
The held voltage, scaled by S&H LEVEL
0V for the first half of each clock cycle and 10V for the second half
A slowly wandering voltage, made by peak-detecting the pink noise and low-passing the result twice

Note — TRIG IN and SYNC IN fire when the whole-volt part of the input goes from zero to anything else, so a swing past -1V triggers them as surely as one past +1V.

V218-SH-Clock-Noise.notes: TRIG IN and SYNC IN are edge-detected on (int)getVoltage(), not on a Schmitt trigger, so the threshold is one whole volt in either direction and a negative swing past -1V is an edge as much as a positive one past +1V. The negative field is left off those two ports because none of ignored, subtracts or swings describes it. SH OUT is written only inside the if(samp) branch, so it holds its last value indefinitely when nothing is patched to GATE IN or TRIG IN. The README's 0.3Hz to 30Hz clock range, the 5ms trigger length and the 20V peak-to-peak white noise are all literals in the code. The README calls the pink filter a -3dB per octave approximation; that figure is not a constant anywhere in the source, so it is not quoted in the lines.
